title: The hypotheses of smooth-proper purity hold for the structure morphism
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and interpret $\Qlb$-objects in the algebraically closed coefficient category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $X_0/k_0$ be smooth, proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses], put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ be the structure morphism. Then:

1. The constructible exceptional inverse image $Ra_X^!$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is defined on the bounded constructible finite-Tor coefficient category [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] at $\Qlb$ and is right adjoint there to the compact-support direct image $Ra_{X!}$ [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]; no ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility hypothesis is imposed.
2. The object $Ra_X^!\Qlb$ carries the canonical functorial Weil structure induced by geometric-Frobenius base change and the adjunction units and counits, so that the pair $(\omega_X,\theta_{\omega_X})$ with $\operatorname{For}(\omega_X)=Ra_X^!\Qlb$ and Weil structure $\theta_{\omega_X}$ this canonical isomorphism is a $\Qlb$-Weil complex on $X_0$ in the sense of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]; this pair is called the dualizing Weil complex of $X_0$.
3. For every integer $i$, the ordinary and compactly supported cohomology groups $H^i(X,\Qlb)$ and $H^i_c(X,\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] are finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces, equipped with the action of the global geometric Frobenius [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius].

source.place: statement, the sentences 'Assume $a_X:X\to\Spec k$ is exceptional-adjoint admissible at $\Qlb$, and choose a dualizing Weil complex $(\omega_X,\theta_{\omega_X})$ with $\operatorname{For}(\omega_X)=Ra_X^!\Qlb$ ... and require $\theta_{\omega_X}$ to be the canonical functorial Weil lift'; and literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-input-weights/thm-weil-deligne-purity.md, statement, 'Assume directly that all displayed cohomology groups are finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces'. These assumptions are discharged by no node; this node states them as a claim for the smooth proper structure morphism.

proof.text: The fixed setting [sk-def-set] uses the constructible exceptional inverse image for every separated finite-type morphism and explicitly imposes no ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility hypothesis. The package theorem [sk-thm-sf-package] states that this constructible $Rf^!$ is right adjoint to $Rf_!$ on the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories, unconditionally. Apply this to the structure morphism $a_X$ and the $\Qlb$ coefficient stage.

The equivariant-operations proposition [prop-weil-operations] gives every constructible exceptional inverse image an equivariant lift whose Weil isomorphism is induced by the corresponding Frobenius exchange and adjunction maps. Applying it to $a_X$ and the constant $\Qlb$ object gives the canonical structure $\theta_{\omega_X}:Lg_X^*Ra_X^!\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_X^!\Qlb$. The underlying object $Ra_X^!\Qlb$ lies in $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ by the typing $Rf^!:\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)\to\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ of step 1, and $\theta_{\omega_X}$ is an isomorphism of $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$, so by the definition of the Weil-complex category [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] the pair $(\omega_X,\theta_{\omega_X})$ is a $\Qlb$-Weil complex on $X_0$ with $\operatorname{For}(\omega_X)=Ra_X^!\Qlb$; this is the pair the statement calls the dualizing Weil complex.

source.place: statement and proof, equivariant lift of $Rf^!$

proof.text: The finiteness theorem [sk-lem-finite] says that at the $E$ and $\Qlb$ field stages the ordinary and compactly supported derived global-section complexes of every bounded constructible finite-Tor object are perfect point complexes, hence have bounded finite-dimensional cohomology. Apply it to the constant $\Qlb$ object on $X$. The equivariant-lift and cohomology assertion in [prop-weil-operations] supplies the induced global geometric-Frobenius actions on both cohomology groups.
